labels.note: Live report that something is broken; Max cannot diagnose, vagueness does not make it hypothetical.
Client asking for time; reversible, unambiguous, send the link with no notification.
Negation rule: the cancel is explicitly disclaimed, and confirming a diary entry asks for no action.
Concrete live defect with reproduction evidence; diagnosis belongs to a person.
Plain request for time; typo does not affect intent.
Explicit negation of the booking ask plus a future contingency; hypothetical rule means no intent.
Data discrepancy is a live problem, and Max may not assert which unverifiable figure is correct.
Bare day proposal is still a scheduling ask; book vs move is unclear but both are lane A.
Negation scoped to its clause: no descope is happening and no question or request is made.
Live outage on the client's own checkout; the sister is evidence, not a third-party subject.
Long message but the only intent is a booking ask with constraints; the past-session gripe is context, not a complaint.
Retraction of a prior instruction; nothing is being moved or cancelled, so no action and no notify.
Failed transaction is a problem and the stuck customer charge is a billing matter; no card number so not PII.
Direct booking ask; extra attendee does not change the lane.
Negation rule: an explicit statement that nothing is being cancelled carries no cancel intent.
Forwarded but the broken system is ours; third-party rule does not apply to a relayed live defect.
Request for a new slot ahead of an existing call; reversible and unambiguous.
Hypothetical outage carries no problem intent, but the buried question about escalation path has a documented non-committal answer.
Live recurring failure with environment detail; hand over, do not attempt diagnosis.
Booking ask with duration and topic; dashboard mention is the agenda, not a problem report.
Hypothetical rule kills the legal intent so no D, but the live question asks Max to assess a timeline, which is a commitment.
Idiom rule: site down is an outage report even in question form.
Request for a session; topic is the agenda, not an intent of its own.
Curiosity framing does not change that answering means stating scope and resourcing for a launch, which Max may not commit to.
Live recurring defect, explicit escalation language demanding an answer, and customer chargebacks.
Booking ask with a proposed slot; the sign-off thanks is not a separate social intent.
Nothing to schedule per the explicit disclaimer; the remaining question is about working process, though it borders on asking for a commitment.
Live data defect; loyalty points are not currency so no money intent.
Ask for a short slot ahead of an existing meeting; send the link.
Third-party rule: the unpaid invoice is with their supplier and explicitly not ours, so no money intent.
Resolved rule: the issue is closed, so no live problem; what remains is an acknowledgement, which gets a reaction not a reply.
Offering availability is a scheduling ask; whether new or a shift, it stays lane A.
Third-party appointment moved, and they state they will still attend, so no move or cancel of our call.
Hedged wording but a real observed discrepancy, which the hypothetical rule treats as a live problem report.
Request for immediate time; send the link rather than leaving them waiting.
Third-party rule: the stray invites belong to another vendor's ended standup, so no cancel or move intent for us and no ask.
Outage report; brevity does not make it ambiguous.
Proposing a session next week; a booking ask.
Third-party rule: an internal audit call moved, explicitly not touching our meeting, so no move intent.
Live payment failure; a card brand plus last four is not a card number, so the PII rule does not fire and this is not lane D.
Unambiguous ask for time today.
Resolved rule: fixed on their side and explicitly withdrawn, so no live problem.
Live customer-facing defect relayed from a colleague about our system.
Booking ask; returns is the agenda topic, not a problem report.
Resolved rule plus an explicit stand-down; the bug is closed so there is no live problem.
Live failing load test with a technical question Max must not answer.
A standing constraint that existing calls must shift off Mondays; a reschedule, not a cancellation.
No referent at all and it asks for confirmation Max cannot verify; intent cannot be determined confidently.
Recurrence of a known defect stated as live now, not as resolved.
Explicit request to shift an existing call.
Implies dropping a planning session without naming one; acting would mean inventing a cancellation, so the unambiguity bar is not met.
Measured live performance failure; hand over rather than explain it away.
Time shift on an existing call; typo is irrelevant.
Idiom rule splits the two uses of down: first is an outage (C), second is agreement plus a slot confirmation (A), so the scheduling action is promoted to B.
Resolved rule: explicitly a false alarm with a cause found, so no live problem and nothing to hand over.
Request to push an existing call; reversible and unambiguous.
Billing question is lane C, and the thanks is a lane A social; multi-intent rule promotes the reaction to B so a person can intercept the money question.
Accumulating live cases plus a diagnosis question Max must not confirm.
Shift request on an existing call.
Idiom self-corrected in the same message: not dead, only delayed on their side, and no question or request is made.
Live storefront defect with a clear reproduction.
Explicit request to move an existing call earlier.
The instruction is to stop something, but the referent is unrecoverable, so the intent cannot be determined confidently.
Live reporting defect contradicted by known facts; a person must investigate.
Reschedule request to a different day.
Going live is scoped by the next clause to an internal Slack channel; no problem, no request, nothing to act on.
Live fulfilment defect affecting a third of labels; hand over.
Reschedule request keeping the time and changing the day.
Politeness masks a live status chase; answering would assert progress or a delivery expectation Max cannot verify or commit to.
Live customer-facing checkout error with evidence.
Attendee conflict on our own call; a reschedule ask, not a third-party matter.
Politeness and a light jab wrap a real booking ask; the tone is warm rather than a churn or escalation signal, so not dissatisfaction-driven scheduling.
Live unresolved discrepancy plus pushback on a prior explanation; Max must not re-diagnose.
Straight swap request; the throwaway pleasantry is not a separate intent.
Sarcasm is a dissatisfaction signal and the time ask is driven by it; book it and flag hard per the lane B scheduling-driven-by-dissatisfaction case.
A new occurrence makes it live despite the hopeful framing; the exasperation is frustration with the bug, not an escalation.
Cancel is act-and-notify per the policy: cancel it, offer rebooking, and post it internally as a health signal.
Praise only; react rather than compose a reply, since a reply here is noise.
Live defect plus real value not deducted, which is a billing matter a person must own.
Skipping a scheduled call is a cancellation; act and notify.
Minimising language does not resolve it; a payment outage is reported with no statement that it is fixed, so it is live.
Resolved rule: explicitly not broken, only delayed, and stated as a correction to close the loop.
Dropping themselves from a booked call is a cancellation of their attendance and the same health signal, so act and notify.
No lawyers, dispute or adversarial wording so not lane D despite the sensitive framing; but it asks for an undertaking Max may not give.
Live customer-facing defect; hedged opening does not make it hypothetical.
Reads as a cancellation of the pending call; act and notify so a person can intercept if the referent is wrong.
The confidential framing is a joke about a colleague's cake; a pleasantry gets a reaction, nothing else.
Live error with a technical cause question Max must not diagnose.
Binning a call is a cancellation; act, offer rebooking, notify.
Downplaying preamble does not change that 200 orders were blocked overnight; a live problem.
Reproducible live inconsistency plus a proposed cause Max must not confirm.
Explicit cancellation; act and notify, third-party absence is only the reason.
No card number so the PII rule does not fire; the payment method on file is still a billing matter, and FYI framing does not make it Max's to answer.
Live defect with a question about intended behaviour that Max cannot answer without asserting an unverified fact.
Cancellation of today's call; act and notify.
Self-contradicting, then explicitly withdrawn in the final clause; the last instruction governs and it is to do nothing.
Live volume of mismatched orders flagged for attention; the promised paste does not defer the handover.
Dropping a scheduled call is a cancellation; act and notify.
Negation correction reverses a release instruction; Max cannot act on deploy timing and a person must own the change.
Resolved rule removes the live incident, but the buried question asks for a root cause Max cannot assert, so it still hands over.
